Maya (CS): Need a tiny customer-facing 'launch quickplay' for a new tenant going live tomorrow. Single page, non-tech, plus an appendix with 3-4 ops commands.
Ravi (Eng): Ok. Make the customer-facing part verbs-only: Check, Prefill, Toggle, Safeguard. Keep examples short.
Marco (PM): Also include a short renewal signal section they can self-check weekly. Simple green/yellow/red rules.
Dana (SRE): For ops appendix: include `curl` health check + thresholds and a simple JS client-batching snippet. Also call out fallback routing to a smaller model and canary advice.
Maya (CS): Draft one-pager copy attempt below. Please poke holes.
Ravi (Eng): minor edits inline.
---
Customer Quickplay: Launch One-Pager (for product teams)
1) Preflight checks (2 mins)
   - Check service health: `curl https://api.redwood/v1/tenants/<id>/health` -> expect `latency_p95 < 400ms`, `error_rate < 0.5%`, `active_sessions > 0`.
   - Confirm warm pool: see `warm_pool_size >= expected_concurrency`
2) Prefill / Warmup (5 mins)
   - Upload top 30 representative prompts or call the prefetch endpoint with prime examples.
   - Mark these calls with note `prefill:true` in telemetry so CS can filter traces.
3) Stream for UI-first flows (optional)
   - Toggle streaming in dashboard for chat-like UX. If your UI needs per-token UI feedback, enable streaming.
4) Cost & safety guard (1 min)
   - Turn on per-route quotas and set a conservative burst limit for first 48h.
5) Weekly quick health (1 min)
   - Green: usage stable or up, avg satisfaction >=4, latency_p95 < 400ms.
   - Yellow: usage down 15-40% OR satisfaction 3-4 OR p95 400-700ms.
   - Red: usage down >40% OR satisfaction <=2 OR p95 > 700ms OR 2+ incidents in 7d.
Feedback micro-form (embed/link)
   - Q1: "Was output useful?" (Yes / No)
   - Q2: "Latency rating" (1-5)
   - Q3: "Anything broken?" (open)
   - Route responses to CS webhook: https://hooks.redwood/internal/cs-feedback (add tenant_id param)
---
Operations appendix (for integrators / infra)
Quick checks
  - Health: `curl -s https://api.redwood/v1/tenants/<id>/health | jq '{p50: .latency_p50, p95: .latency_p95, err: .error_rate}'`
  - If `err > 0.01` for 10m -> trigger fallback and page oncall.
Fallback example (YAML style)
  - `route: conversational`
  - `fallback:`
  - `  model: small-infer-v1`
  - `  max_tokens: 256`
  - `  rollout: {canary_percent: 5, duration: 24h}`
Client batching snippet (JS)
```javascript
// naive client-side batching: flush after 40ms or 200 tokens
let buf = [];
let start = null;
function enqueue(msg){
  if (!start) start = Date.now();
  buf.push(msg);
  if (tokenCount(buf) > 200 || Date.now() - start > 40){
    sendBatch(buf);
    buf = []; start = null;
  }
}
```
Troubleshooting quick hits
  - Streaming stalls: compare `client_timeout` vs `server_chunk_timeout` (increase client timeout by 2x as quick test).
  - Warm pool not populating: ensure prefill calls have `prefill:true` and that cache TTL > 30m during ramp.
  - P95 spikes after launch: look for long context windows, background eval jobs, or plugin timeouts.
Telemetry tips
  - Tag prefill traces with `prefill:true` and `test_session:true` where applicable.
  - Add `route` and `tenant_id` to every span to make dashboards filterable.
---
Renewal-risk signals (quick):
  - Low usage + low satisfaction -> high risk.
  - Repeated performance regressions (p95 >700ms) -> medium/high risk.
  - Survey trend: negative comments mentioning accuracy or cost -> flag for AE.
---
